subject: Bayesian analysis for fractions of mortality

messages.author: 10e17346e14a0eac
messages.subject: Bayesian analysis for fractions of mortality
parts:
We run a program to retrieve and necropsy manatee carcasses.  These necropsies are used in part to assign cause of death to each carcass.  We divide cause of death into seven categories: watercraft, water control structures, entanglement, cold stress, red tide, other, and undetermined.  As usual in such things, there are a significant number of undetermined.  One issue with ignoring those in estimating fractions of mortality is the cause of death may affect one’s ability to determine the cause of death; in other words, the undetermined carcasses may have different probabilities of death causes than the known carcasses.  We are trying to estimate the overall fractions of mortality between the known causes of death (first six), incorporating our uncertainty about the undetermined deaths. 

The person who held my position two people before me, Chris Fonnesbeck, developed a fairly simple Bayesian model for estimating these fractions.  He implemented it in Python (PyMC), and I’m trying to translate it into JAGS (or OpenBUGS or WinBUGS), but having some problems.  Here is one way of describing the model (further simplified to ignore details of region, year, and age):

u(i) ~ Multinomial(U, p(i))

x(i) = u(i) + y(i)

x(i) ~ Multinomial(U+Y, pi(i))

where U is the total number of undetermined carcasses, u(i) is the number of those that died of cause i, p(i) is the probability for cause i for the undetermined carcasses, y(i) is the number known to have died of cause i, Y is the total number died of determined causes, and pi(i) is the overall probability of cause i.  pi and p are given vague Dirichlet priors (all ones). 

You can probably anticipate the problem I originally had in JAGS: I’m trying to define x twice, which it doesn’t allow.  With Andy Royle's help, I figured out a way around that - I can model y(i) as the sum of x(i) and -u(i) using the dsum function.  Then it didn't like my dmulti calls (Error: Unable to find appropriate sampler), so I replaced them with individual dpois calls and used dsum to tie them together to the totals.  Now it runs, but doesn't converge.  In fact, the values for x and u never budge from their starting values.

Any suggestions for implementing this model?  Is there a way to do this in JAGS or should I learn Python or try to code my own MCMC in R?  I've attached my R/JAGS code.  I can send the link to the Python code if you're interested.

Thanks,

Jeff
